To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the brain stem provides periodicity to the sympathetic outflow to the kidney and spleen, and that the sympathetic outflow from the brain stem to the kidney and to the spleen is not the same as that to the hindlimb.
the sympathetic activities of the rat are differentially affected by spinal transection, and that brain stem systems can synchronize the activities of the abdominal sympathetic outflows.
spinal transection doubles renal and splenogastic sympathetic activities, but it does not change lumbar activity, and it abolishes synchronization of renal and splenognastic activities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of sympathetic nerve activity in rats.
the control of sympathetic activity.
the neural mechanisms that control sympathetic nerve activities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
brain stem systems can synchronize sympathetic nerve activities and can maintain sympathetic activity in some nerves after spinal transection.
brain stem systems can provide synchronization of abdominal activities, and that these activities can be generated independently in both intact and spinal animals.
the spinal cord is not necessary for sympathetic nerve activity, and that the brain stem is not the only source for the generation of sympathetic nerve activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain stem is not essential for the maintenance of sympathetic activities in the rat.
brain stem systems are capable of modulating, but not controlling, abdominal sympathetic activities.
the brain stem and spinal cord contain parallel pathways that control the same effector organ.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain stem can be a source of sympathetic activity that can influence renal and splenic sympathetic nerve activity, but it is not the only source.
the brain stem is important for the coordination and modulation of sympathetic activities, but not for maintaining the sympathetic activities per se.
the sympathetic nervous system is not a single system.
